title: WebAssembly
summary: WebAssembly (Wasm) is a portable binary and text format for executable programs, designed as an open standard to enable high-performance applications on web pages and beyond. It functions as a structured stack machine with control flow expressed through constructs like blocks, ifs, and loops. While initially focused on low-level languages like C and C++, subsequent versions added features such as multithreading, SIMD, and garbage collection to support high-level language runtimes. The format maps to a common structure from multiple concrete representations, primarily binary and text formats.

mechanisms.title: Binary and Text Format Mapping
mechanisms.explanation: WebAssembly defines a binary code format and a corresponding text format that both map to a common internal structure. This dual representation allows for efficient parsing and human-readable development, with the binary format serving as the executable unit processed by runtimes.

mechanisms.title: Structured Stack Machine Semantics
mechanisms.explanation: WebAssembly operates as a structured stack machine where most computations use a value stack, but control flow is expressed in structured constructs such as blocks, if statements, and loops. Implementations need only behave as if a value stack and control structures exist, rather than maintaining them literally.
